If you're ever in Australia and get the chance, try yabbies (they're a fresh water crustacean). Beautiful just boiled, with a bit of salt, pepper and white vinegar added. If you're up north (NT or northern WA) try Barramundi (a fish). Not worth wasting your time if you're down south as it's all tasteless. You can obviously try our other unique meats (kangaroo, emu, crocodile), but they're not that good IMO. Also if you get a chance try a sausage from one of our sausage sizzles (pretty much the Australian equivalent of the hot dog). It's a barbecued sausage in a slice of bread with some fried onions and tomato sauce (our version of ketchup). Obviously there are some more well know Aussie foods as well, like Vegemite (which most non-Aussies I know, dislike) and Pavlova (technically a NZ food, but we claim it; way too bloody sweet in my book).

There's some foods that aren't unique to Australia, but also aren't common in most countries I've visited. Meat pies and sausage rolls (again with tomato sauce) are good examples. Make sure you get one from a genuine bakery, not the shit from a supermarket or football stadium. Chicken Parmigianas (chicken schnitzel topped with Neapolitan sauce and cheese) is our standard pub fare. There are also some foods that are definitely not unique to here, but that we do better :-P A lamb roast (leg of lamb, roast spuds, roast onions, etc., with mint sauce) is one of our famous ones; our fish & chips are also bloody awesome (find a wog or Yugoslav fish & chip shop if you want the best).

Beverage wise I can't think of anything we have that others don't. Most people I know outside of the bush prefer foreign beers. People rave about our wines (especially our Shiraz and wines from the Barossa Valley region), but personally I'd prefer a French/Spanish/Italian red and a Marlborough (NZ) Sav Blanc for a white. One soft drink (soda) I noticed absent in a lot of European countries is our lemon squash (Solo is the best one IMO). We also have a rum distillery up north (Bundaberg), but that stuff tastes like shit if you're used to good quality south/central American rums (I'll probably be shot by some bogans for saying that :-P ).

The facts are this:

  • In a duty to retreat state (which Ohio is) self defense is not an affirmative defense for using deadly force when you are outside your home.

  • In a stand your ground state, self defense is an affirmative defense to using deadly force basically anywhere.

If this had occurred in a stand your ground state, the victim would have an affirmative defense of self defense if charges were brought against him. In this case the victim would likely prevail if charges were brought against him. In Ohio however, the victim cannot claim self defense in this shooting even though his life was threatened by armed robbers because he stepped outside his home. He now has to battle criminal charges and has a good chance of being convicted.
